plan: In a single-round auction with values drawn from $0-$20, a dominant strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. With a value of $13, I want to win if possible, but minimize my payment. Other rational bidders will likely bid similarly. I'll aim to bid around $11-$12 - high enough to likely win, but low enough to potentially create a profitable margin if my bid is the second highest.

In a second-price sealed bid auction with values between $0-$20, the optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value. Since my value is $6, I want to bid strategically. Other bidders will likely bid near their true values. A bid slightly above my value (around $7-$8) balances winning probability with minimizing overpayment. This approach maximizes expected profit by increasing chances of winning while not significantly risking losing money.

In a single-round sealed bid auction with values between $0-$20, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly less than my true value. Since my value is $13, I want to win without overpaying. Other rational bidders will likely bid similarly. I'll aim to bid around $10-$11 to create a buffer that increases my chances of winning while protecting potential profit margin. This strategy balances winning probability with minimizing potential overpayment.
